The essay text below each prompt is a complete response. The learning notes after it are commentary and should not be included in an exam answer.
M1 Cheaper consumer goods
Task: People can now buy cheaper consumer goods. Do the advantages outweigh the disadvantages?
Read after your own attempt | 276 words in the essay

Many everyday products have become more affordable, allowing households to buy items that were once beyond their budgets. Although this can improve living standards, I believe the disadvantages outweigh the advantages when low prices encourage excessive consumption of short lived goods.

The main benefit of cheaper products is wider access to useful items. A family with a limited income may be able to afford a refrigerator, a computer or essential furniture without borrowing heavily. These purchases can make daily life easier and support work or education. Lower prices may also leave more money available for other needs, such as transport and housing. It would therefore be unreasonable to regard affordable goods as undesirable in themselves, particularly for households that previously struggled to obtain basic equipment.

However, the more serious problem is the pattern of consumption that low prices can encourage. When replacing an item costs little, customers may discard it instead of repairing it. For example, someone might repeatedly buy inexpensive clothing that loses its shape quickly rather than maintaining a smaller collection of durable clothes. Producing and disposing of these items uses materials and creates waste, so the effects extend beyond the individual buyer. Frequent replacement can also reduce the financial saving that attracted the customer initially. These repeated costs are more significant than the brief satisfaction of making an unnecessary purchase, especially when many consumers behave in the same way.

In conclusion, affordable products clearly help people meet important needs. Nevertheless, I consider the wider costs of excessive buying and frequent disposal to be greater where cheap goods are treated as replaceable. The strongest benefits come from affordability combined with durability and thoughtful purchasing.
What to notice
The judgement compares repeated social costs with individual benefits; it does more than count points. Notice the qualification about short lived goods.
M2 Shopping as a leisure activity
Task: In many places, shopping is becoming a free time activity, replacing traditional hobbies. Discuss the reasons for this development. Is it positive or negative?
Read after your own attempt | 295 words in the essay

Shopping is increasingly treated as entertainment rather than simply a way to obtain necessary goods. This change is partly explained by attractive shopping environments and consumer marketing. Although shopping can be enjoyable, I regard the trend as largely negative when it displaces other valuable activities.

One reason for this development is that shopping centres offer much more than shops. Restaurants, cinemas and comfortable indoor spaces allow visitors to spend several hours in one location. For groups of friends, this can be an easy meeting place, especially when outdoor conditions are unpleasant. Marketing also encourages people to associate purchases with enjoyment and personal success. Repeated exposure to new products and limited time offers may make browsing feel exciting even when a person has no practical need to buy anything. Together, these features help explain why shopping competes with established leisure pursuits.

There are some positive aspects to this change. People can relax, meet friends and make useful purchases during the same visit. However, problems arise when spending becomes the main source of recreation. A young person who regularly buys fashionable items may exceed a reasonable budget, while receiving only temporary satisfaction from each purchase. In addition, time spent visiting shops can replace exercise, creative hobbies or community activities that develop skills without requiring continual consumption. These alternatives offer benefits beyond owning another product. Shopping is therefore less desirable as a dominant hobby than as one occasional part of a varied leisure routine.

In conclusion, the growth of shopping as entertainment reflects both the design of shopping centres and the influence of marketing. While it can provide a convenient social experience, I believe its increasing replacement of other hobbies is generally negative because of the pressure it creates on personal budgets and the use of free time.
What to notice
Body paragraph 1 explains reasons. Body paragraph 2 evaluates the trend. Both the introduction and conclusion give the same overall judgement.
M3 Food waste
Task: Nowadays, people tend to waste a great amount of food. Why is this happening, and how can we solve this problem?
Read after your own attempt | 280 words in the essay

A considerable amount of food is purchased or prepared but never eaten. Two avoidable causes are poor planning before shopping and serving portions that are too large. More careful purchasing and greater flexibility over portion sizes could help reduce this waste.

Poor planning often leads households to buy more perishable food than they can use. Shoppers who do not check their cupboards may purchase items they already have, while special offers can encourage them to buy quantities that exceed their needs. Some of this food then spoils before it is eaten. Oversized portions create a similar problem after food has been prepared. At home or in a restaurant, people may serve a standard large amount without considering an individual’s appetite. If the remaining food is discarded rather than stored safely or shared, the ingredients and effort used to prepare it are wasted.

The solutions should address these two stages directly. Before shopping, households can check existing supplies and plan a realistic number of meals. A list based on those meals makes it easier to avoid unnecessary purchases, although it should allow for changes in plans. People can also serve smaller initial portions and offer more food when needed. Restaurants could support this approach by providing different portion sizes, allowing customers to choose an amount they are likely to finish. These actions do not require everyone to follow an identical diet; they simply bring the quantity purchased or served closer to the quantity actually needed.

In conclusion, food waste is often connected to decisions made before shopping and before serving a meal. Checking supplies, planning purchases and offering suitable portions can reduce these avoidable losses by dealing with their immediate causes.
What to notice
Each solution matches a cause: shopping lists address overbuying, and flexible portions address uneaten servings. The conclusion adds no new solution.
M4 Skilled workers leaving poorer countries
Task: Professionals such as doctors and teachers are leaving poorer countries for developed countries to advance their careers. What problems arise, and what solutions can be suggested?
Read after your own attempt | 289 words in the essay

When trained doctors and teachers move from poorer countries to wealthier ones, their home communities may lose essential expertise. This can weaken public services and place additional pressure on remaining staff. Better working conditions and credible career opportunities are important ways to reduce these problems.

The most immediate difficulty is a shortage of experienced professionals. A hospital that loses several doctors may struggle to maintain appointments, while a school with fewer teachers may have to increase class sizes. The remaining workers can face heavier workloads, making their jobs less attractive and potentially encouraging further departures. There is also a longer term loss when experienced staff are no longer available to train newer colleagues. Replacing one departing professional therefore involves more than filling a vacancy: institutions may also need to rebuild practical knowledge and supervision. These pressures can make it harder to provide reliable services, particularly in areas that already have few specialists.

Governments and employers should respond by making local careers more sustainable. Competitive and reliably paid salaries can help, but professionals also need appropriate equipment, manageable workloads and opportunities to develop their skills. For example, a teacher may be more willing to remain in a school that offers useful training and a clear route to promotion. Where resources are limited, improvements could initially target institutions with the greatest staffing shortages. Partnerships with professionals abroad may also support temporary teaching, mentoring or return placements, allowing some expertise to benefit the home country even when permanent return is unlikely.

In conclusion, professional emigration can reduce service capacity and weaken the training of future workers. Improving employment conditions and creating ways for overseas professionals to contribute would address these problems more constructively than simply expecting people to abandon their career ambitions.
What to notice
The first body paragraph explains consequences. The second proposes responses. It does not treat migration itself as wrongdoing.
M5 Respect for older people
Task: In many countries there is insufficient respect for older people. What are the reasons, and what problems might this bring to society?
Read after your own attempt | 284 words in the essay

Older people do not always receive the consideration or recognition they deserve. Reduced contact between generations and narrow ideas about social value may contribute to this problem. The consequences can include weaker support for older adults and fewer opportunities for younger people to learn from them.

One possible cause is the limited time that family members spend together. When work and study schedules rarely overlap, younger relatives have fewer chances to hear older people’s experiences or understand their needs. Physical distance can make regular contact harder as well. Another factor is the tendency to judge people mainly by current earnings or familiarity with new technology. In settings where these qualities are valued above everything else, retired people may be unfairly regarded as having little to contribute. Such assumptions overlook the unpaid care, practical knowledge and community involvement that many older adults provide.

This lack of respect can affect both individuals and wider relationships. Older family members may be excluded from decisions that concern them, or their requests for support may receive little attention. This can contribute to isolation and make everyday difficulties harder to manage. Younger generations also lose opportunities for learning when they dismiss older people’s views without listening. For example, family conversations can pass on knowledge about local history, work and relationships that is difficult to obtain from a textbook alone. Respect does not require unquestioning agreement with every traditional belief, but it does require treating the speaker as someone whose experience deserves consideration.

In conclusion, weaker contact between generations and an overly narrow view of personal worth can contribute to disrespect towards older people. This can reduce support for older adults and weaken the exchange of knowledge within families and communities.
What to notice
This is a causes and effects response. It does not replace the requested effects with a long list of solutions.
M6 Dangerous sports
Task: Dangerous sports should be banned. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Read after your own attempt | 283 words in the essay

Some people believe that sports involving a high risk of injury should be prohibited. Although the risks deserve serious attention, I disagree with a general ban. Adults should normally be able to choose challenging activities, while organisers should be required to manage foreseeable dangers responsibly.

The first reason is that participation can offer benefits that a blanket prohibition would remove. Activities such as climbing require preparation, discipline and cooperation, and some people find meeting these challenges highly rewarding. An informed adult may reasonably decide that these experiences justify a degree of personal risk. This does not mean that every activity should be permitted in every setting. The important distinction is between a participant accepting a risk and exposing other people to danger without their consent. Rules can address the latter without removing all opportunities for voluntary participation.

Supporters of a ban correctly point out that serious accidents can occur. However, prohibition does not directly improve training, equipment or supervision, and some participants may continue in less regulated settings. A more useful response is to set standards suited to the activity. Organisers could require appropriate instruction, check equipment and cancel events when conditions are unsafe. Beginners could also be restricted to routes or activities suitable for their experience. These measures cannot eliminate risk, but they target preventable causes of injury while preserving a legal environment in which standards can be monitored. Where a particular practice cannot be made acceptably safe, a narrower restriction may still be justified.

In conclusion, the possibility of injury is a reason for careful regulation rather than an automatic ban on all dangerous sports. Informed choice, appropriate supervision and targeted restrictions provide a more proportionate response to the risks involved.
What to notice
The counterargument is acknowledged fairly. The response explains why regulation is preferable, rather than claiming that danger is harmless.
M7 Domestic priorities and international aid
Task: It is impossible to help all people in the world, so governments should focus on people in their own countries. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Read after your own attempt | 294 words in the essay

Governments have limited resources, and it may be unrealistic for them to meet the needs of every person worldwide. However, I disagree that this means they should concentrate exclusively on their own populations. Domestic priorities can coexist with targeted international assistance.

There are sound reasons for recognising practical limits. The scale of need can exceed available budgets, while different communities require different forms of support. Providing food after a disaster, for instance, involves different arrangements from improving a school system over several years. Governments also have responsibilities to maintain essential services for their own citizens. If hospitals or public infrastructure at home are seriously underfunded, leaders must consider those needs when deciding how much assistance they can offer abroad. Acknowledging these constraints is more realistic than suggesting that any single country can solve every problem through additional spending.

Nevertheless, the inability to help everyone is not a convincing reason to help no one outside national borders. A limited contribution can still make a substantial difference when it addresses a clearly identified need. Countries may provide emergency supplies, specialist staff or funding through coordinated programmes, sharing the burden rather than acting alone. International assistance can also support common interests because crises do not always remain within one country. For example, disruption to regional transport or food supplies may affect neighbouring populations as well. Carefully chosen cooperation can therefore be both a humanitarian response and a practical investment in wider stability, provided that spending is transparent and results are monitored.

In conclusion, governments should recognise the limits of their resources and protect essential domestic services. Yet these duties are compatible with helping people elsewhere. The sensible response is to set priorities and cooperate, rather than treat universal assistance and complete national isolation as the only choices.
What to notice
The essay accepts limits in claim A but rejects the exclusive conclusion in claim B. Alternative positions are outlined in the Handle opinion questions carefully section.
M8 Building function and appearance
Task: When designing a building, its use is more important than its outward appearance. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Read after your own attempt | 291 words in the essay

The design of a building must account for both its practical purpose and the way it looks. I do not agree that one should always receive greater importance. Safety and usability are essential, but appearance can also be central to a building’s value and its relationship with the surrounding area.

Function clearly deserves close attention because a building must serve the people who use it. A school needs suitable classrooms, accessible routes and spaces that support learning. Similarly, an office requires an arrangement that allows staff to work effectively. Attractive decoration cannot compensate for poor ventilation or an inaccessible entrance. The financial consequences of ignoring these needs can also be substantial if alterations become necessary after construction. Designers should therefore establish practical requirements early and ensure that visual choices do not undermine them. In particular, safety should never be sacrificed merely to create a striking exterior.

At the same time, appearance is not necessarily a superficial extra. Buildings form part of a shared public environment, so their design affects people beyond their owners. A well designed library or community centre can create a welcoming impression and fit comfortably with nearby streets. In an area with distinctive historic architecture, an insensitive exterior may also weaken the character that residents value. These considerations need not demand an extravagant budget. Proportion, materials and a thoughtful relationship with the surroundings can improve appearance while remaining compatible with efficient use. The strongest designs integrate these features instead of treating practical and visual aims as competing projects.

In conclusion, a building must be safe and fit for its purpose, but its appearance can also make a lasting contribution to public space. Both deserve serious attention, with the balance determined by the building’s users, location and intended role.
What to notice
The response qualifies the comparison rather than ignoring it. “Function” includes use and accessibility, not merely interior decoration.
M9 Government and private scientific research
Task: Scientific research should be carried out and controlled by governments rather than private companies. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Read after your own attempt | 296 words in the essay

Scientific research can serve public needs as well as commercial goals. I agree that governments should provide strong oversight and support important areas of research. However, I disagree that they should replace private companies as the organisations carrying out all scientific work.

Government involvement is necessary because some valuable research may offer little immediate commercial return. Investigations into environmental protection or basic scientific questions can take many years to produce a practical application. Public funding allows researchers to pursue such work without depending entirely on the prospect of selling a product. Governments also have a responsibility to establish ethical requirements and independent review, particularly where research affects people or the environment. Clear standards, transparent reporting and scrutiny of results can help protect the public regardless of who pays for a study. Oversight is therefore an essential public role, although public institutions themselves also require accountability.

Private companies nevertheless have useful capabilities that should not be excluded. They may possess specialist equipment, experienced teams and the resources needed to turn a research idea into a usable product. A business developing more efficient industrial equipment, for example, can test whether an invention works under everyday production conditions. Commercial incentives may encourage rapid development, but they can also create pressure to present favourable results. This risk supports the case for disclosure, independent testing and effective regulation; it does not establish that every private project should be prohibited. Cooperation between public researchers and businesses can combine different strengths when responsibilities and safeguards are clearly defined.

In conclusion, governments should guide research priorities where public needs are neglected and enforce appropriate standards across the sector. Private companies should still be able to conduct research within that framework. Shared participation with accountable oversight is preferable to giving either sector an unrestricted monopoly.
What to notice
Distinguish who conducts research from who regulates it. The position remains consistent from the introduction to the conclusion.
M10 The best way to improve road safety
Task: The best way to improve road safety is to increase the minimum legal age for driving cars or riding motorbikes. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Read after your own attempt | 294 words in the essay

Raising the minimum driving age is sometimes proposed as the best way to make roads safer. Although such a policy could limit some inexperienced drivers’ exposure to risk, I disagree that it is necessarily the most effective response. Broader measures should address unsafe behaviour and driving conditions across age groups.

An age restriction has a limited reach because it changes who may drive, rather than ensuring that all drivers behave safely. Drivers above the new threshold could still speed, ignore signals or use a phone while travelling. The policy would not directly address poor road markings or dangerous junctions either. In addition, young adults who need to commute may face difficulties where reliable public transport is unavailable. These concerns do not prove that age is irrelevant to driving ability. They show, however, that raising the threshold cannot on its own resolve the range of factors involved in road safety, so its value must be compared with other available interventions.

A stronger approach would combine practical training, consistent enforcement and safer infrastructure. Training can help new drivers recognise hazards and develop appropriate judgement before travelling independently. Enforcement should focus on dangerous conduct, with proportionate penalties that discourage repeated violations. Meanwhile, maintaining road surfaces and improving crossings can reduce risks for drivers and pedestrians alike. These actions affect a much wider range of journeys than an age change alone. Better public transport may further help by providing an alternative when someone is unable to drive safely. The appropriate mix will depend on the problems observed in each location.

In conclusion, increasing the driving age may have a role in a wider safety policy, but it should not automatically be regarded as the best solution. Measures targeting skills, behaviour and road design offer a more comprehensive response.
What to notice
The task asks whether this is the best approach. The essay acknowledges a possible benefit, then compares the proposal with wider measures.
M11 Government action on housing shortages
Task: The shortage of housing in big cities can cause severe consequences. The only way to solve this problem is government action. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Read after your own attempt | 291 words in the essay

A shortage of suitable housing can place serious pressure on city residents. Government action is essential because public authorities influence planning, infrastructure and support for low income households. Nevertheless, I disagree that government action alone is the only way to address the problem effectively.

Public authorities have responsibilities that cannot simply be left to individual businesses. They can decide where housing is permitted, coordinate transport and utilities, and provide support for people who cannot afford market prices. Without this coordination, new homes may be built far from jobs or without adequate services. Governments can also protect minimum building standards and invest directly where private supply is insufficient. These roles are especially important because a larger number of housing units does not automatically mean that homes are affordable or suitable for those facing the greatest need. A successful policy must consider who can use the additional supply.

However, private developers and community organisations can contribute to achieving these goals. Developers bring construction capacity and investment that may expand the supply more quickly than public building programmes alone. Their contribution needs clear planning rules and incentives that support the types of homes actually required. Community housing groups can also identify local needs and participate in projects designed around residents rather than short term sales. For example, a cooperative may organise shared spaces and manage a development collectively. Such arrangements still depend on a supportive public framework, but the construction, financing and management involve several actors rather than the government acting alone.

In conclusion, government has a central role in tackling housing shortages, particularly through coordination and protection of vulnerable residents. Yet lasting improvement can also depend on private investment and community participation. The most convincing approach combines these contributions under clear public objectives.
What to notice
The disagreement concerns “only”. The essay explains a central government role without contradicting its support for shared action.
M12 Grandparents and childcare centres
Task: Some working parents think grandparents can take care of their children, while others believe childcare centres provide the best care. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
Read after your own attempt | 300 words in the essay

Working parents often need help caring for young children, and both grandparents and childcare centres can provide valuable support. Each option has advantages, but I favour care by grandparents when they are willing, capable and supported. The quality of the arrangement matters more than its label.

Childcare centres appeal to many parents because they can offer a regular schedule and organised activities. Children have opportunities to play with peers and learn how to share materials or follow group routines. A well run centre may also have staff trained in early childhood care, making it easier to plan activities suited to different stages of development. These benefits are particularly useful when relatives live far away or cannot provide daily care. However, parents still need to consider staffing, supervision and the individual child’s needs. The existence of a centre does not itself guarantee that its care is appropriate.

Grandparents may provide a different strength: a familiar relationship and close attention to the child’s everyday preferences. Care at home can offer continuity, especially for a young child who finds changes in routine difficult. Grandparents may also share family stories and customs through ordinary conversations and activities. These advantages explain my preference when the arrangement works for everyone involved. Nevertheless, it would be unfair to assume that all grandparents have the energy, time or desire to provide full time care. They may need practical support, and children can still benefit from opportunities to socialise outside the home. Safety and care quality must be considered in either setting.

In conclusion, childcare centres can provide structured activities and reliable support, while grandparents may offer familiarity and individual attention. I would prefer family care when suitable, but parents should base the final decision on the child’s needs and the actual quality and sustainability of the available options.
What to notice
Both views receive a fair explanation. The preference is qualified, avoiding unsupported claims that either setting guarantees safety.
M13 Longer prison sentences and alternatives
Task: Some people think the best way to reduce crime is to give longer prison sentences. Others believe there are better alternatives. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
Read after your own attempt | 293 words in the essay

Longer prison sentences are often proposed as a way to reduce crime, while others argue for alternative responses. Imprisonment has an important role in protecting the public from dangerous offenders. However, I believe crime reduction also requires measures that address the reasons people offend and support their return to society.

Supporters of longer sentences argue that keeping serious offenders in custody protects potential victims for a longer period. This is a clear consideration where someone presents a continuing danger to others. A substantial sentence may also communicate the seriousness with which society regards an offence. These arguments explain why imprisonment remains necessary in some cases. Nevertheless, the length of a sentence alone does not determine whether an offender will change their behaviour. If a person leaves custody without practical skills, support or a realistic means of earning a living, simply having served more time may not address the difficulties they face afterwards.

Alternative approaches can target these problems more directly. Education, vocational training and carefully planned support after release may help suitable offenders establish a lawful routine. For less serious offences, supervised community service can impose a meaningful consequence while allowing a person to maintain employment and family responsibilities. Prevention is important as well: supporting young people who are at risk of leaving education without useful skills may reduce some pressures associated with offending. None of these measures is appropriate for every person or offence, so decisions need to reflect the seriousness of the conduct and the risk to the public.

In conclusion, longer imprisonment can be justified for dangerous offenders, but it should not be treated as the best response to every form of crime. A combination of proportionate punishment, rehabilitation and prevention offers a more complete approach to reducing future offending.
What to notice
The model discusses both views and gives a clear judgement. It avoids claiming that prison duration alone guarantees rehabilitation or deterrence.
M14 Western clothing and traditional dress
Task: In many countries, people now wear Western clothes such as suits and jeans rather than traditional clothing. Why is this? Is it a positive or negative development?
Read after your own attempt | 300 words in the essay

Western styles of clothing have become common in many places where traditional dress was previously more prominent. Practical demands, widespread availability and media influence help explain this shift. I consider it largely positive for everyday choice, provided that traditional clothing continues to have a place in cultural life.

One reason is that many workplaces and schools use clothing styles that are convenient to standardise. Trousers, shirts and similar items are widely available in different sizes and can be adapted to a range of activities. International retail networks make these products easy to obtain, while films, advertising and social media increase their visibility. People may therefore choose them both because they are practical and because the styles feel familiar. This does not mean that traditional clothing is always uncomfortable or unsuitable. Rather, purchasing habits and workplace expectations can make widely sold alternatives the easiest option for everyday use.

The main benefit is the flexibility that a broad choice of clothing gives individuals. A person can select affordable, durable items suited to their work, travel and leisure activities without needing a different outfit for every occasion. Shared styles may also make shopping more convenient when people move between countries. The potential drawback is that local forms of dress may receive less attention, reducing opportunities to learn about their history and craftsmanship. However, everyday adoption of international styles does not require abandoning traditional clothing entirely. Cultural events, family celebrations and education can provide meaningful settings in which such clothing is worn and understood, rather than treated simply as a costume with no explanation.

In conclusion, convenience, availability and cultural influence help explain the popularity of Western clothing. The trend is generally beneficial when it expands personal choice, while efforts to maintain knowledge of traditional dress can preserve an important connection with the past.
What to notice
The first body paragraph answers why; the second evaluates the change. The overall positive judgement allows a clearly explained cultural limitation.

E4A Population growth

Rapid population growth can create serious problems for cities. When the number of residents increases faster than the supply of homes, families may struggle to find affordable accommodation. For example, more car journeys can worsen air quality if public transport does not expand, while inadequate waste collection can leave rubbish in public spaces. These problems depend partly on how well infrastructure keeps pace with demand.

E4B Schools and parents

Encouraging children to share responsibilities or resolve disagreements calmly gives them repeated practice outside the classroom. These roles support each other because children can apply school learning in family life and bring habits developed at home into their relationships with classmates.
Check the development: One example supports the role of schools and another supports the role of parents. The final sentence explains what “complementary” means in this context.

P1 Shopping malls
Task: Nowadays young people like spending much of their free time in shopping malls. Do the advantages of this development outweigh its disadvantages?
Suggested complete response | 284 words

Shopping malls have become popular places for young people to spend their free time. They provide convenient spaces for meeting friends and enjoying entertainment. However, I believe the disadvantages outweigh these benefits when shopping becomes a dominant leisure activity, particularly because of the pressure on personal budgets and time.

There are understandable reasons for enjoying a visit to a mall. Several facilities are available in one place, so friends can meet for a meal, see a film or browse shops without arranging separate journeys. Indoor spaces may also be convenient when the weather makes outdoor activities uncomfortable. Some young shoppers can practise making sensible decisions by comparing prices and following a fixed budget. These experiences show that a mall visit does not have to involve excessive spending. Used occasionally, it can be a useful part of a varied social routine.

The difficulties arise when frequent visits encourage people to purchase things they do not need. Promotions and displays can make a small purchase seem harmless, yet repeated spending can consume a substantial part of a limited budget. A student who regularly buys new clothes may have less money for transport or educational materials. There is also an opportunity cost: time spent shopping can replace exercise, creative projects or inexpensive community activities. These alternatives develop skills and relationships without requiring continual purchases. Since the financial and time costs can recur every week, they may be more significant than the temporary pleasure of buying another product.

In conclusion, shopping malls offer convenient entertainment and social opportunities, but these benefits do not justify allowing shopping to dominate young people’s leisure time. The disadvantages are greater when repeated visits create unnecessary spending and crowd out more varied activities.
Check the answer

Outweigh essay. Possible view: The disadvantages are greater when shopping takes up too much leisure time. Limit: Do not assume every mall visit involves buying goods. Vocabulary: impulse purchases; consumer spending; leisure activities.
P2 Threats to animal species
Task: Animal species are becoming extinct due to human activities on land and in the sea. What are the reasons and solutions?
Suggested complete response | 291 words

Human activities are placing many animal species under pressure on land and in the sea. Habitat destruction and excessive exploitation are two important causes. Protecting living environments and controlling the use of wildlife resources are therefore necessary responses, particularly when these measures are backed by effective monitoring.

On land, clearing forests for development or production can remove the places where animals feed and reproduce. A species may struggle even if some forest remains, because isolated areas can make it harder to find food or suitable breeding partners. In marine environments, intensive fishing can reduce populations faster than they recover. When large numbers of animals are removed repeatedly, future reproduction may also decline. These pressures are different from a single temporary disturbance: they can persist over time and affect the conditions needed for a population to survive. Pollution can further damage habitats, adding to the difficulty of recovery.

The solutions need to address these causes directly. Public authorities can protect important habitats from damaging development and restore connections between remaining areas. For example, preserving a breeding site is more useful than declaring an unrelated area protected simply because it is available. Fishing authorities can also set limits appropriate to local conditions and check that those limits are followed. Monitoring catches and enforcing restrictions give the rules practical effect. Communities and businesses that depend on these resources should be involved, because conservation is more sustainable when people understand the rules and have workable alternatives to harmful practices.

In conclusion, species decline is often connected to the loss of suitable habitats and the removal of animals at unsustainable rates. Protection, restoration and properly enforced limits can reduce these pressures. Announcing conservation goals alone is insufficient without the resources and cooperation needed to implement them.
Check the answer
Causes and solutions. Match each response to a source of harm. Limit: A protected area needs management, not just a name. Vocabulary: habitat loss; overexploitation; conservation (bảo tồn).
P3 Antisocial behaviour
Task: These days, there has been an increase in antisocial behaviour and a lack of respect for people. What are the causes and what solutions can be taken?
Suggested complete response | 282 words

Antisocial behaviour and disrespect can make everyday life more difficult for the people affected. Inconsistent guidance about acceptable conduct and weak responses to harmful behaviour may contribute to these problems. Education in respectful interaction, combined with fair enforcement, can help address the causes rather than merely condemn the results.

One possible cause is that some children receive little consistent guidance about managing disagreement. If aggressive behaviour is ignored or modelled by adults, young people may not learn more constructive ways to express frustration. Schools cannot fully compensate when expectations at home are unclear. Another factor is the response to misconduct in public settings. When harassment or intimidation is repeatedly overlooked, those responsible may believe there are few consequences. People affected may also stop reporting incidents if they expect no useful response. This does not mean that every instance has the same cause, but it helps explain how harmful patterns can continue.

Parents and schools can respond by teaching and demonstrating practical alternatives. Children need opportunities to practise listening, resolving conflicts and recognising how their actions affect others. Clear expectations should be applied consistently, while mistakes can become opportunities for learning. Authorities and organisations also need accessible reporting procedures and proportionate consequences for serious misconduct. For example, a transport provider could make it easier to report harassment and ensure that complaints receive a timely response. These measures support people affected and show that rules are meaningful, without treating every disagreement as a criminal matter.

In conclusion, inadequate guidance and ineffective responses can contribute to disrespectful behaviour. Teaching constructive interaction and enforcing clear standards are complementary solutions. Their value depends on consistent practice by families, institutions and the authorities responsible for protecting the public.
Check the answer

Causes and solutions. Focus on behaviour such as harassment, aggression or public disorder. Limit: Avoid blaming an entire generation or treating quietness as antisocial behaviour. Vocabulary: social norms; parental guidance; law enforcement.
P4 Work life balance
Task: Not many people are able to achieve a balance between work and other aspects of life. What are the problems? What solutions can be suggested?
Suggested complete response | 293 words

Many people struggle to balance employment with family responsibilities, rest and other activities. The resulting problems include weaker personal relationships and limited opportunities to recover from demanding work. Employers and households can help by setting reasonable boundaries and distributing responsibilities more fairly.

One consequence of poor balance is the loss of shared time with family and friends. A worker who is regularly available to colleagues during evenings may be physically at home but unable to participate fully in conversations or activities. Over time, this can weaken the support that close relationships provide. Insufficient rest can also make it harder to concentrate and manage daily demands. The problem may be especially difficult when paid work is combined with an unequal share of domestic tasks. A person responsible for most childcare or housework may have fewer opportunities to develop professionally or simply take a break. These consequences affect more than the individual’s schedule; they influence relationships and participation in working life.

Employers can improve the situation by reviewing workloads and making expectations about contact hours clear. A formal right to leave work is of little use if employees are still expected to answer routine messages throughout the evening. Managers should therefore plan tasks realistically and respect agreed boundaries. At home, family members can discuss the division of domestic responsibilities and adjust it to their circumstances. Sharing recurring tasks can protect time for rest and prevent one person’s career from being consistently treated as less important. Flexible working arrangements may help where they support these practical changes.

In conclusion, poor work life balance can undermine relationships, recovery and career opportunities. Reasonable employment expectations and a fairer distribution of household responsibilities address these problems together. Successful change requires boundaries that people can actually maintain in everyday life.
Check the answer

Problems and solutions. Discuss consequences, rather than using the whole first paragraph for causes. Limit: A pay rise alone may not reduce excessive hours. Vocabulary: support network; household responsibilities; career development.
P5 Less family time
Task: People are spending less time with their family members. What are the reasons for this phenomenon? What effects does it have?
Suggested complete response | 287 words

Family members in some households have fewer opportunities to spend time together. Conflicting schedules and individual use of digital entertainment help explain this change. Its effects can include weaker emotional support and fewer chances for children to receive everyday guidance, although the outcome depends on how families maintain contact.

The first reason is that work and study commitments often occur at different times. Parents may return home late, while children have lessons or assignments that occupy their evenings. Even when everyone lives in the same house, finding a period for a shared meal can be difficult. A second reason is that available leisure time may be spent separately on screens. Someone watching videos or exchanging messages with distant friends may pay little attention to relatives nearby. Technology can certainly connect family members who live apart, but it can also displace conversation when it becomes the default activity during time that could be shared.

Reduced interaction can make it harder for relatives to notice when someone needs support. A problem at school or work may remain unspoken if there is rarely a relaxed opportunity to talk. Children may also have fewer chances to observe how adults deal with disagreements or responsibilities. Such learning often happens through ordinary routines rather than formal advice. However, less time together does not automatically mean that a family is uncaring. Short but attentive conversations and regular shared activities may preserve strong relationships. The quality of interaction therefore matters alongside its frequency.

In conclusion, busy schedules and separate digital routines can reduce shared family time. This may weaken support and everyday learning if meaningful contact is lost. The most serious effects arise when limited time is accompanied by limited attention to one another’s needs.
Check the answer

Reasons and effects. Keep the causal chain visible. Limit: Online communication can also help relatives who live apart. Vocabulary: family bonding (gắn kết gia đình); competing priorities; emotional support.
P6 Fair university access

Task: Some people think everyone has the right to access university education and governments should provide places for all students, no matter their financial background. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Suggested complete response | 289 words

A person’s financial background should not decide whether they can attend university. I largely agree that governments should support fair access to places. However, this should mean removing financial barriers for suitable applicants, rather than assuming that every person must enter a university regardless of their preparation or interests.

The strongest reason for public support is that cost can prevent capable students from continuing their education. An applicant from a low income household may meet admission requirements but struggle to pay tuition or living expenses. If the opportunity is lost solely because of money, both the student and society may miss the benefits of their potential. Grants, affordable student support and suitable accommodation can reduce these barriers. For example, assistance with living costs may be as important as tuition support for someone who must move away from home. Fair access requires attention to the actual expenses that prevent participation.

Nevertheless, governments also need to consider educational capacity and suitability. University courses require resources and appropriate prior preparation, so providing a place without support or relevant prerequisites may not lead to successful study. Some people also prefer vocational training or employment routes that match their goals more closely. These choices should receive serious support rather than be presented as inferior alternatives. Governments can expand opportunities while maintaining clear admission standards and investing in several forms of further education. This approach respects the right to pursue learning without treating university as the only worthwhile destination.

In conclusion, financial circumstances should not exclude eligible students from higher education, and governments have an important role in making access fair. The policy should combine practical financial support with suitable places and alternative pathways, so that opportunity reflects ability and interests rather than household income.
Check the answer

Opinion. Possible view: Support access based on ability and interest, without financial exclusion. Limit: Financially fair access is not automatically universal free tuition or admission without prerequisites. Vocabulary: financial background; eligibility; targeted support.
P7 Internet access and achievement
Task: Internet access helps young people and workers achieve their education and work goals more easily than before. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Suggested complete response | 287 words

Internet access has made many educational and professional goals easier to pursue. I largely agree with this view because online resources broaden learning opportunities and digital communication reduces barriers to collaboration. However, these advantages depend on reliable access, relevant skills and the ability to manage distractions.

For learners, the internet provides access to explanations, courses and practice materials beyond those available locally. A student who does not understand a classroom explanation can revisit the topic through another presentation and work at a suitable pace. This can be especially helpful when a specialist subject is not offered nearby. Search tools also make it easier to locate information for projects, although students must assess its reliability. The advantage is therefore more than simply obtaining material quickly: learners can choose resources that match their needs and return to them when necessary. Effective use still requires active practice rather than passive viewing.

Workers benefit from easier communication across distances. Colleagues can share files, discuss a proposal in a video meeting and coordinate a project without travelling to the same office. These possibilities reduce some time and transport costs and make it easier to involve people with different expertise. Nevertheless, being connected does not guarantee success. Frequent notifications can interrupt concentrated work, while unreliable connections may make remote participation difficult. Digital skills and clear working routines are therefore needed to turn access into an actual improvement. People without suitable devices or connections may gain less than others.

P25 Newspapers and other media
Task: Some people think newspapers are the best way to get news. Others believe other media platforms are better. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
Suggested complete response | 300 words

People can obtain news through newspapers, broadcast services and digital platforms, each with particular strengths. Some prefer newspapers for detailed reporting, while others value the convenience and speed of other formats. I believe the best choice depends on the reader’s purpose, with reliability being more important than the medium itself.

Newspapers can offer a focused selection of stories with background and editorial organisation. A reader may find it easier to consider a detailed article when it is presented without constant notifications or competing short posts. Editorial checks can also help clarify complex information and provide context beyond an immediate update. These features explain why some people regard newspapers as the strongest source. However, they are not guarantees of accuracy, and newspapers differ in their standards and priorities. Many also publish online, so the value often lies in the reporting organisation and its methods rather than paper as a physical format.

Other media platforms can be more suitable when information needs to reach people quickly. Broadcasts and digital services can provide updates, maps or video that help explain a developing event. They may also be easier to access during travel or for readers who prefer listening. The challenge is that fast circulation can allow unreliable claims to spread alongside verified information. Users should therefore consider who produced a report and whether it has been checked. A credible digital publication may be more useful than a poorly reported newspaper, just as a careful newspaper investigation may offer more context than a brief social media post.

In conclusion, newspapers provide advantages in depth and focused reading, while other platforms offer speed and varied presentation. No format is best for every situation. Readers should choose suitable media while prioritising transparent reporting, verification and context, rather than assume that reliability follows automatically from the format.

Task: Nowadays, people tend to waste a great amount of food. Why is this happening, and how can we solve this problem?
Suggested complete response | 280 words

A considerable amount of food is purchased or prepared but never eaten. Two avoidable causes are poor planning before shopping and serving portions that are too large. More careful purchasing and greater flexibility over portion sizes could help reduce this waste.

Poor planning often leads households to buy more perishable food than they can use. Shoppers who do not check their cupboards may purchase items they already have, while special offers can encourage them to buy quantities that exceed their needs. Some of this food then spoils before it is eaten. Oversized portions create a similar problem after food has been prepared. At home or in a restaurant, people may serve a standard large amount without considering an individual’s appetite. If the remaining food is discarded rather than stored safely or shared, the ingredients and effort used to prepare it are wasted.

The solutions should address these two stages directly. Before shopping, households can check existing supplies and plan a realistic number of meals. A list based on those meals makes it easier to avoid unnecessary purchases, although it should allow for changes in plans. People can also serve smaller initial portions and offer more food when needed. Restaurants could support this approach by providing different portion sizes, allowing customers to choose an amount they are likely to finish. These actions do not require everyone to follow an identical diet; they simply bring the quantity purchased or served closer to the quantity actually needed.

In conclusion, food waste is often connected to decisions made before shopping and before serving a meal. Checking supplies, planning purchases and offering suitable portions can reduce these avoidable losses by dealing with their immediate causes.
